body:
I don't think this is really a problem. If you have commented out code or a comment mentioning a specific class, it can be useful to have a tooltip for it. You can also ctrl+click these to go to the documentation, which can also be useful. It seems like it would be inconsistent to only remove the tooltip for it and not the ctrl+click behavior.
It's only with generically named classes that are capitalized like this that it may be unexpected. But I don't think that is enough of a reason to remove it. 
You have to pause your mouse on top of the word for a second for the tooltip to open, so it shouldn't accidentally happen often either.

I have actually been thinking about allowing this for non-script files even.
